summary: Pakistan issues tourist eVisas through its official online portal to citizens of the 192 countries on its eligibility list — with fees of USD 8.18 to 60 depending on nationality — and citizens of the six Gulf Cooperation Council states need no visa at all. Indian citizens apply for a visit visa at the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi.

fee.notes: Set by nationality. The portal's fee calculator gives, for a single-entry tourist visa of up to 3 months: USD 20 for most eligible nationalities (100 of 192); USD 25 for 31 mostly Asian and Gulf states; USD 35 for most of Europe and Latin America; USD 50 for Germany; USD 60 for the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Mexico; and USD 8.18 for ten countries including China, Japan, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. No nationality is shown as fee-free.

currencyLimits.text: Travellers may bring foreign currency notes into Pakistan without limit. Pakistani rupees are limited to PKR 10,000 per person in or out (PKR 3,000 to or from India). A general permission lets anyone take foreign currency out up to USD 10,000 per visit for adults, USD 5,000 for ages 5–18 and USD 1,000 for children under 5 (or the equivalent); visitors not ordinarily resident in Pakistan may also take out the unspent foreign currency they brought in, if their stay has not exceeded three months.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Pakistan's economy is primarily cash-based and that credit cards are accepted by some larger establishments. ATMs are available in the main cities but may not accept foreign debit cards; currency can be exchanged at all international airports.

It says the local authorities at your destination will tell you if you need a No Objection Certificate.

tips.text: Apply on the official portal visa.nadra.gov.pk. For a tourist entry visa it asks for a photograph, your passport and hotel booking details.

The UK FCDO says you must get advance permission from local or federal authorities to travel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan and several districts of Azad Kashmir, that there are prohibited areas around military installations, and that local authorities sometimes arrange a police escort in higher-risk areas.

TravelHealthPro says that if you stay in Pakistan for 4 weeks or more, you may be asked on departure for proof of polio vaccination on an ICVP, given 4 weeks to 12 months before you leave, and that without it you may be vaccinated on departure.

The UK FCDO advises men and women to cover their shoulders and legs in public, and women to cover their heads in mosques, holy places and rural areas. During Ramadan it advises not eating, drinking or smoking in public in the daytime.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Pakistan?
faq.answer: Almost everyone does. Citizens of the 192 countries on the official eligibility list can apply online for a tourist eVisa at visa.nadra.gov.pk — the fee, set by nationality, is USD 8.18 to 60. Citizens of the six GCC states (Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates) do not need a visa. Indian citizens apply for a visit visa at the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi.

faq.question: How long does the Pakistan eVisa take?
faq.answer: The portal gives the processing time for a tourist entry visa as 7–10 working days, or 4 weeks for Afghan and Somali passport holders. If the application is sent back to you for review, the processing time starts again from the date you resubmit it.

faq.question: Can Indian citizens visit Pakistan as tourists?
faq.answer: Indian citizens apply for a visit visa at the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi. It asks for details of each place to be visited, an attested invitation from a sponsor in Pakistan for each city, and a fee of Rs. 120 per entry. No official source we could read says whether tourist visits are granted.

faq.question: Can I enter Pakistan on an Israeli passport?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states whether Pakistan admits travellers on Israeli passports.

faq.question: Is Pakistan safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO advises against all travel within 10 miles of the Afghan border and to Balochistan and parts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and against all but essential travel to Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
